key_insight: A high-throughput computational search identified 58 CuI-based ternary candidates for p-type transparent conductors and generalized design rules beyond oxide systems.
engineering_relevance: These materials could expand transparent hole-conducting options for tandem photovoltaics and transparent electronics, though solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Search X–Cu–I crystal structures using minima hopping and density functional theory.
Filter candidates for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Analyze Cu coordination and electronic states to refine valence-band design rules.
evidence_signal: Of 58 predicted candidates, 49 were previously unreported and 20 were intrinsically p-type degenerate semiconductors; Cu₂FI₂ had a calculated 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m₀ hole effective mass.
watch_item: Computational predictions require experimental validation of synthesis, transparency, conductivity, and device compatibility.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
